items.text: REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the tax law and the state finance law, in relation to video
lottery gaming in the town of Woodbury
items.lawCode: Amd §§1612 & 1617-a, Tax L; amd §54-l, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6525

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law and the state finance law,
in relation to video lottery gaming in the town of Woodbury

 
PURPOSE:

To maintain the State video lottery gaming revenue previously coming
from video lottery gaming operations Monticello racetrack by authorizing
a video lottery gaming facility to be operated in Orange county by the
owner of Monticello racetrack. Also enhances existing racing support
payments and ensures the long-term continuation of harness racing at
Monticello racetrack, while providing for mitigation payments to the
operator of video lottery gaming operations at Yonkers racetrack.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Provides for a vendor fee of 46% for the new video lottery
gaming facility authorized by this act.

Section 2: Clarifies that the Orange county video lottery gaming facili-
ty is not a vendor track.

Section 3: Provides that, as consideration for being granted the author-
ization to operate the video lottery gaming facility in Orange county,
the operator of such facility shall provide racing support payments in
to Monticello racetrack (8.75% to purses and 1.25% to breeders) and to
Yonkers racetrack an amount to maintain purses for horsemen at the same
dollar levels realized in 2018, adjusted by the consumer price index for
urban consumers. Additionally, 1.25% of total revenue wagered at the
facility after pay out for prizes, shall be distributed to the appropri-
ate breeding fund for the manner of racing conducted by such track.

Section 4: Authorizes the Gaming Commission to issue a video lottery
gaming license to the entity that operated the video lottery gaming
facility at Monticello racetrack to operate a facility in Orange county
and: (a) prohibits such entity from operating a video lottery gaming
facility at both locations, (b) requires continued racing operations at
Monticello racetrack in order to ensure the long-term continuation of
harness racing at Monticello track; (c) requires such Orange county
facility to be at least 30 miles from the video lottery gaming facility
at Yonkers racetrack; (d) requires the operators of the Orange County
facility and the video lottery gaming facility at Yonkers racetrack to
enter into a mitigation agreement, to be approved by the gaming commis-
sion, that addresses, (i) a mitigation payment to the operator of the
video lottery gaming facility at Yonkers racetrack and (ii) the require-
ment of such mitigation to be in place in order to operate the facility
in Orange County. Additionally, as the condition of the license to oper-
ate a video lottery gaming facility in the Town of Woodbury, the opera-
tors must maintain staffing levels at their commercial gaming facility
in Sullivan County at levels no less than 90% of the staffing levels at
the commercial gaming facility as of the end of the third quarter of
2019. The license operators must also maintain quarterly assistance
payments to the Village of Monticello, the Town of Thompson and Sullivan
County, at the same levels made in 2018 to be adjusted annually pursuant
to changes in the consumer price index for urban consumers.


Section 5: Makes all municipalities within which the new video lottery
facility will be located in eligible for state assistance in accordance
with Section 54-1 of the state finance law.

Section 6: Effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Tax Law sections 1612 and 1617-a authorize Monticello racetrack to oper-
ate VLT machines and distributes the net win from such machines as
follows:

* 41% vendor fee (less 10% in racing support payments for purses and
breeders);

* 39% State education aid;

* 10% marketing allowance;

* 10% gaming administration to the State Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering
and Breeding Law section 1351 provides a 39% tax on casino gross gaming
revenue (of which 80% is allocated to State education aid and 20% to
local tax relief).

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Montreign Operating Company, LLC d/b/a Resorts World Catskills and
Monticello Raceway Management, Inc., the owner/operator of Monticello
Casino and Raceway - together under the Empire Resorts corporate umbrel-
la - are Sullivan County's largest employer with over 1,600 employees.
To provide sustainability to the business, Empire Resorts seeks statuto-
ry authorization to relocate its current VLT allocation to a location
with a more stable revenue base. The proposal would authorize Monticello
Raceway to move its video lottery gaming facility to Orange County. This
will provide the State with incremental video lottery gaming revenue and
enhanced racing support payments and long-term continuation of harness
racing at Monticello racetrack.

This legislation relies on maintaining Monticello Raceway's effective
tax rate in 2018 but seeks no tax breaks or additional incentives. The
Orange County video lottery gaming facility would be restricted to a
site that is more than 30 miles from Yonkers racetrack in order to maxi-
mize revenue potential. This legislation also requires Empire Resorts to
enter into an agreement with MGM Yonkers in order to provide mitigation
payments to address projected revenue cannibalization.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

The proposed video lottery gaming facility would contribute approximate-
ly $23M of incremental revenue directly to the State (for education and
administrative expenses of the gaming commission) and will result in
significant direct capital investment in Orange County with direct
employment of over 300 permanent jobs and additional construction and
induced jobs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided however, that no video
lottery gaming may be conducted at any facility within Orange County
unless and until the mitigation agreement required by this act is
executed by all parties and approved by the gaming commission.
